test_title: PYST 33: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 23 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
If after being bitten by a mosquito, the person is detected as being malaria positive, which of the following will hold true?

A. The person did not have a balanced diet.

B. The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.

C. The mosquito was suffering from malaria.

D. The person was not vaccinated as a child.
solution:
The correct answer is __**The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Malaria is caused by **Plasmodium parasites**, which are transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• The mosquito acts as the **vector** for the Plasmodium parasite, carrying and transmitting it to humans during a blood meal.
 
• Only female Anopheles mosquitoes are capable of transmitting malaria because they require blood to produce eggs.
 
• Plasmodium parasites include several species, such as **P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, and P. ovale**, with P. falciparum being the most deadly.
 
• Without the presence of Plasmodium in the mosquito, a mosquito bite does not result in malaria transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium Life Cycle:**

 
 
• Plasmodium parasites undergo a complex life cycle involving both humans and mosquitoes.
 
• The parasite's **sporozoites** are injected into the human bloodstream during a mosquito bite.
 
• In humans, the parasite first infects the liver before moving to red blood cells, causing the symptoms of malaria.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Malaria:**
 
 
• Common symptoms include fever, chills, headache, nausea, and muscle pain.
 
• Severe malaria can result in complications such as organ failure, cerebral malaria, or death.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Malaria:**
 
 
• Use of insecticide-treated mosquito nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS) can reduce mosquito exposure.
 
• Preventive medications, such as antimalarial drugs, are recommended for travelers to malaria-endemic areas.
 
 
 
• **Global Malaria Control Efforts:**
 
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) leads initiatives like the **Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030** to reduce malaria cases and deaths.
 
• Malaria vaccine research, such as the RTS,S vaccine, is progressing as a potential tool for prevention.
